p: A bit of planning goes a long way with any outdoor battle game, and the first question to settle is who is actually coming. Mixed groups work best when everyone is roughly up for the same level of rough and tumble, so if you have a couple of nervous first-timers alongside the self-declared tactical geniuses, mention it when you book. Operators can usually pitch the games to suit, and a good briefing at the start means nobody feels out of their depth.

Think about food and drink too. Running round a field is thirsty work, and a big bottle of water each plus something to snack on between rounds keeps energy and tempers in check. If it's a birthday or a stag, sorting where you're eating afterwards before the day saves a lot of hungry dithering in a muddy car park.

Newnham itself is worth a proper look once the battle is done. The village has a long, handsome high street running along the riverbank, and the Severn here is wide, tidal and moody, with sweeping views over to the Cotswold edge on a clear day. This is also Severn Bore country, the famous tidal wave that surges up the river on the biggest tides, so if you're curious, look up the predicted bore dates before you travel.

Gloucester is a short drive up the A48 for a bigger choice of food and shops, and the wider Forest of Dean is all around you for walks and cycle trails the next day, which is handy if the group fancies stretching sore legs out gently.
